solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the blog titled it No 21952, which the sequence puts at 29152

entries.clue: No great distance to north: others on the move in south-west (6,5)

indicatorNotes.on the move: letters that are on the move will not stay in the order given
indicatorNotes.in: the jumbled letters sit inside, between S and W

blocks.note: S for south, the compass point, opening the outer shell
W for west, the compass point, closing the shell

annotation.surface: Directions for a short walk: nip north, while the others wander about down in the south-west.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To' is fodder, not a link: the anagram takes TO, N and OTHERS together, and the result sits between the two halves of south-west.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the distance you could lob a stone, so a very short way.

entries.clue: Short jacket turned up in bag (3)

indicatorNotes.Short: a word that is short falls one letter shy of full length
indicatorNotes.turned up: in a down clue, turning up reads the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: CASE, a jacket or casing, cut short

annotation.surface: A cropped jacket has turned up stuffed in someone's bag.
annotation.walkthrough: A jacket in the potato or book sense is an outer case, which is the synonym needed here.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from biology: a pouch-like cavity in a plant or animal.

entries.clue: Magical land with a certain invigorating air (5)

blocks.note: the land of the Wizard of Oz

annotation.surface: A fairy-tale land with a bracing atmosphere.
annotation.walkthrough: The Victorians believed the sharp smell of the seaside was a gas that did you good, and the name stuck to fresh, bracing air.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose, informal sense: the fresh, stimulating air of the seaside.

entries.clue: Perhaps Gladstone’s rising importance in surrounding area? (7)

indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, something rising reads upwards
indicatorNotes.surrounding: to surround something is to enclose it, so IN wraps around A

blocks.note: a person of note has importance; it is then turned upwards

annotation.surface: A question about whether the Victorian prime minister Gladstone was growing in stature in his district.
annotation.walkthrough: Gladstone, four times Prime Minister, was schooled at the famous English public school by the Thames, so 'Perhaps' marks him as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Gladstone went to Eton College, so he is one of its old boys.

entries.clue: Display too much creative work around restaurant (9)

indicatorNotes.around: turned around, so the whole string is read backwards

blocks.note: to air something is to display it

annotation.surface: Someone is overdoing the artwork on show in a restaurant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Around' comes last and governs everything before it, not just the nearest word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the informal, family-run Italian eating house.

entries.clue: River Fleet swelled with hot eastern current (5)

indicatorNotes.swelled with: something swelled with extra matter grows to hold it inside

blocks.note: the Royal Navy, split to hold the rest
H (hot) + E (eastern) + I (current, the symbol in physics)

annotation.surface: The Fleet, a London river, swells with a warm current from the east.
annotation.walkthrough: The Fleet is a buried river in London, which makes it look like part of the definition; here it is the navy.
annotation.definitionFit: The German spelling of the Rhine, Europe's great river.

entries.clue: Good-for-nothing succeeded entering temple on lake (7)

indicatorNotes.entering: something entering a place goes inside it, so S goes into WAT
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, a piece that is on another sits below it

blocks.note: a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia, split to take S
the abbreviation used in family trees
L for lake, as on maps

annotation.surface: A layabout has made it into a temple by a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' works twice here: once as a word meaning about, and once placing the lake below it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an idle, wasteful person who is good for nothing.

entries.clue: Lost bird taking off close to castle ditch (3)

indicatorNotes.taking off close to: the close of a word is its end, and taking it off removes the last letter

blocks.note: a castle's ditch, minus its last letter T

annotation.surface: A bird wanders off from a castle moat.
annotation.walkthrough: The giant flightless bird of New Zealand was hunted out centuries ago, which is why it is 'lost'.
annotation.definitionFit: Lost here means extinct: the giant New Zealand bird died out around 1400.

entries.clue: Kinky game involving a learner in study in college (9)

indicatorNotes.Kinky: something kinky is twisted, so the letters are bent out of order
indicatorNotes.involving: to involve something is to take it in, so the jumbled GAME wraps around the rest
indicatorNotes.in: a thing in a study sits inside it, so AL goes inside DEN

blocks.note: GAME rearranged, split to hold the rest
a den is a study, split to hold AL

annotation.surface: A racy game with a learner in a college study.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cambridge college is pronounced 'maudlin'. There are two containers, one inside the other.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: one of the colleges of Cambridge University.

entries.clue: Immortal heart in a man at sea (11)

indicatorNotes.at sea: confused, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A man at sea whose heart will never die.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole of 'heart in a man' is fodder, even though 'in' looks like a container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary word for undying, from the amaranth, a legendary flower that never fades.

entries.clue: Clown dead having consumed hot bean product (9)

indicatorNotes.having consumed: what has been consumed is inside, so COCO takes H in

blocks.note: Coco the Clown, a famous circus clown
H for hot, as on taps

annotation.surface: A clown has died after eating a hot bean dish.
annotation.walkthrough: The clown takes H before LATE follows, though the clue names 'dead' first. Cocoa beans are the beans in question, not baked beans.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: it is made from roasted cacao beans.

entries.clue: Athenian character making the case for Simonides? (5)

annotation.definition: Athenian character making the case for Simonides?

blocks.note: the surface wants a person from Athens; the setter means a Greek letter
the surface wants a lawyer defending the poet; the setter means the Greek S, which begins and ends SimonideS, its case

annotation.surface: An Athenian personality stands up to argue in defence of the poet Simonides.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Character' means letter and 'case' means the outer letters of a word, so the Greek S is the letter that encloses the Greek poet's name.
annotation.definitionFit: Sigma is the Greek S, a letter Athenians wrote, and it opens and closes Simonides.

entries.clue: Boots perhaps initially muddy I placed in trunk (7)

indicatorNotes.initially: what comes initially comes first, so take the first letter of muddy
indicatorNotes.placed in: things placed in a trunk go inside it

blocks.note: a trunk is a chest, split to hold the rest

annotation.surface: Muddy boots are being packed away into a trunk.
annotation.walkthrough: Boots is a big British chain of pharmacies, so 'perhaps' makes it one example; the surface wants them to be footwear.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Boots is Britain's best-known high-street pharmacy chain.

entries.clue: Demand the writer’s rough and hearty in old game show (4,2,5)

blocks.note: to call for is to demand
the writer is me, so the writer's is my
a bluff manner is rough and hearty

annotation.surface: Someone demands a blunt, hearty tone from the author of a TV quiz script.
annotation.walkthrough: The long-running BBC panel game had teams offering true and false definitions of obscure words.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name: the BBC panel game that ran on and off from 1965 to 2005.

entries.clue: Enlightened state’s new stories written on Irish victory (7)

indicatorNotes.written on: in an across clue, words written on another follow it, so ANA comes after IR V

blocks.note: ana is a collection of anecdotes or stories

annotation.surface: A state that has become enlightened publishes new tales about an Irish triumph.
annotation.walkthrough: Ana, a collection of sayings or anecdotes, is a crossword staple; it survives as the ending in words like Victoriana.
annotation.definitionFit: A religious term: in Buddhism, the final state of perfect enlightenment and release.

entries.clue: Bloom left sharp object after first part of Ulysses (5)

indicatorNotes.after: in an across clue, what comes after is written to the right, so PIN follows U
indicatorNotes.first part of: the first part of a word is its opening letter

annotation.surface: Leopold Bloom leaves a sharp object near the opening of James Joyce's Ulysses.
annotation.walkthrough: Leopold Bloom is the hero of Joyce's Ulysses, so the surface reads as literary criticism; Bloom here is just a flower.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a tall garden flower with spikes of pea-like blooms.

entries.clue: Contestant’s history embracing life cut short? (9)

indicatorNotes.embracing: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so PAST wraps around the rest
indicatorNotes.cut short: a word cut short loses its tail, the last letter

blocks.note: your history is your past, split to hold the rest

annotation.surface: A quiz contestant's life story, including a life cut tragically short.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not on your nelly' means 'not on your life': in rhyming slang, Nelly Duff is puff, and puff is breath or life. So NELLIE stands for life.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose fit: panel-game players compete on a quiz panel.

entries.clue: Hardy’s villain periodically consumed by envy? (9)

indicatorNotes.periodically: something done periodically happens at regular intervals, so take every other letter
indicatorNotes.consumed by: something consumed is taken inside, so the letters go into RESENT

blocks.note: to resent is to envy, split to hold the rest

annotation.surface: A villain in a Thomas Hardy novel is eaten up with envy from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: Hardy looks like Thomas Hardy the novelist, but it is the adjective meaning tough.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: tough, able to take knocks and recover.

entries.clue: Wise man covers relic damaged in desecration (9)

indicatorNotes.damaged: the letters of relic are broken up

blocks.note: a sage, split to hold the rest

annotation.surface: A wise man shields a relic broken during an act of desecration.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is almost a straight description of the answer: a damaged relic is itself the act.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: violating something held sacred.

entries.clue: Mr White in Chamonix around on time to see attraction there? (4,5)

indicatorNotes.around: to go around something is to enclose it, so M BLANC surrounds ON T

blocks.note: M for Monsieur, the French Mr

annotation.surface: A Monsieur Blanc in Chamonix, turning up on time to go sightseeing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Chamonix' makes both Mr and White French: M. Blanc. 'There' points back to Chamonix, the resort beneath the mountain.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by location: Western Europe's highest peak towers over Chamonix and draws its visitors.

entries.clue: Pierce and Oscar separating horse from trap (7)

indicatorNotes.separating: O goes between the other two

blocks.note: a bay is a reddish-brown horse

annotation.surface: Pierce and Oscar step in to part a horse from its carriage.
annotation.walkthrough: Pierce looks like a man's name to go with Oscar; it is the verb. A trap is also a light horse-drawn cart, which feeds the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb from the weapon: to stab with the blade fixed to a rifle.

entries.clue: Something fragrant consecutive characters brought to India (5)

blocks.note: EL and EM, the letters L and M spelt out, next to each other in the alphabet

annotation.surface: A string of scented goods shipped to India.
annotation.walkthrough: Letters can be spelt out as words: EL, EM, EN and so on. Any neighbouring pair is 'consecutive characters'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a fragrant tree resin used in perfumes and varnishes.

entries.clue: Returning piano taken into first-rate city shops (7)

indicatorNotes.Returning: going back the way it came, so the whole string reads upwards
indicatorNotes.taken into: something taken into another is put inside it, so P goes into ROME

blocks.note: the city, split to hold P
p for piano, soft in music

annotation.surface: A piano sent back is accepted into the city's best shops.
annotation.walkthrough: A1 is written with I standing for 1, a common crossword swap.
annotation.definitionFit: A plural: large stores, the Latin plural of emporium.

entries.clue: Corporation finished in such a position? (5-2)

blocks.note: a corporation is an old joke word for a pot belly

annotation.surface: A company that has gone bust.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a business failing, which is what going belly-up means; 'such a position' is lying on your back, like a dead fish.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: dead fish float on their backs, so a failed company is said to go this way.

entries.clue: One in wheeled carriage brings dad to Paris (5)

indicatorNotes.in: what sits in a pram is inside it, so I goes into PRAM

blocks.note: a baby's pram, split to hold I

annotation.surface: A dad pushes a baby in a pram on a trip to Paris.
annotation.walkthrough: Paris is the Trojan prince, not the French city: his father was the King of Troy.
annotation.definitionFit: Greek myth: the King of Troy fathered Paris, whose elopement with Helen began the Trojan War.

entries.clue: Progress here impossible, four to leave showing no emotion (7)

indicatorNotes.to leave: letters that leave a word depart from it, so IV is taken out

annotation.surface: A deadlock where four people walk out stony-faced.
annotation.walkthrough: Four is a Roman numeral here, not a head count.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a deadlock or dead end, where nobody can move forward.

entries.clue: Two short ways to make wooden strip (5)

annotation.surface: Two shortcuts to making a strip of wood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two short ways' gives both pieces: two abbreviated road names.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain sense: one of the curved wooden planks that make up a barrel.

entries.clue: Something nasty afoot where bachelor joins this association? (5)

indicatorNotes.joins: the letter joins the answer to make the thing named, so the answer is that thing with the letter taken away

blocks.note: a painful swelling on the foot

annotation.surface: Something nasty is going on, where a single man signs up to this society.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: add B to the answer and you get BUNION. 'Afoot' is literal: on the foot.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trade union or club is an association of members.

entries.clue: Drunk from Britain fuddled with Ecstasy twice (9)

indicatorNotes.fuddled: confused, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: E for the drug ecstasy, twice

annotation.surface: A drunk from Britain, befuddled after taking ecstasy twice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fuddled' fits the drunken surface while telling you to jumble the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal noun for a habitual drinker, from the Latin for made drunk.

entries.clue: Partake of repast odd characters have left (3)

indicatorNotes.odd characters have left: the odd letters go, leaving the even ones

annotation.surface: Guests share a meal after the strange characters have gone home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Odd characters' reads as eccentric people leaving; it means letters 1, 3 and 5.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to partake of food is to consume it.

entries.clue: Corpulent Liberal to be extracted from apartment (3)

indicatorNotes.to be extracted from: something extracted is pulled out, so L is taken out of the word

annotation.surface: An overweight Liberal politician is to be evicted from his flat.
annotation.walkthrough: The Liberals were a major British party, and L is their standard abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: corpulent is the formal word for having a large, stout body.

entries.clue: Character to invite round guys on time (11)

indicatorNotes.round: to go round something is to encircle it, so TEMPT surrounds the rest
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, a piece on another is written after it

blocks.note: to invite, as in to tempt fate; split to hold the rest
an era is a period of time

annotation.surface: A question of whether it is in someone's nature to have the lads round in good time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On time' is not ON + T here: 'on' is a placement word, and the T comes from the end of tempt.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a person's nature or disposition.
